Q: Configure depth overflow value - Start-Job A:

Not an answer that would solve the problem but rather an informative one; the accepted answer from Sage Pourpre is indeed the best solution, don't use recursion at all.

The issue is due to Job's being assigned very small stack size. You could use a PowerShell instance instead of Start-Job, which already gives you a bigger stack thus handling more levels of recursion (by a big amount):

Technique Iterations PowerShell Version Operating System
Start-Job 226~ 5.1 Windows 10
Start-Job 2008~ 7.2.1 Linux
PowerShell Instance 4932~ 5.1 Windows 10
PowerShell Instance 11193~ 7.2.1 Linux
  • Code to reproduce
$iters = @(0)
$script = '& {param($e) $e[0]++; & $MyInvocation.MyCommand.ScriptBlock $e } $args[0]'
$instance = [powershell]::Create().
    AddScript($script).
    AddArgument($iters)

$instance.Invoke()
$instance.Dispose()
$iters

As for the question:

Is there a way to configure the depth overflow value when using Start-Job?

No, not possible, the stack size is defined before the job is started and can't be changed; but something perhaps nice to know is that you can give your runspace a bigger stack using a custom thread, the downside is that this is only applicable if you're doing it in C#... might be possible to do it in pure PowerShell but not sure. Check out this gist for a test comparison.

int stacksize = 123; // TBD in bytes!!

Thread thread = new(() =>
{
    using Runspace rs = RunspaceFactory.CreateRunspace();
    rs.ThreadOptions = PSThreadOptions.UseCurrentThread;
    rs.Open();

    using PowerShell ps = PowerShell
        .Create(rs)
        .AddScript("... TBD ...");

    ps.Invoke();
    // handle errors etc...
}, stacksize);

thread.Start();
thread.Join();

Q: Python try...except comma vs 'as' in except A:

The "as" syntax is the preferred one going forward.

However, if your code needs to work with older Python versions (2.6 is the first to support the new one), then you'll need to use the comma syntax.

Q: How to trigger jenkins build upon bitbucket pull request merged A:

When you configure GIT - push, commit... etc hooks, be sure to check the JENKINS git selection, and set the BRANCH to check for (** specifies all branches) and most importantly,

USE localtunnel.me or similar to set your JENKINS online or it won't work.

Q: Javascript to simulate "right click on image -> save image as" A:

According to the technical specifications of the Document Object there is no method that will allow you to force download a document/file/resource through JavaScript.

Q: How to sort a table on the count of unique items in a field? A:

Just tried this in MySQL, and with this query:

SELECT e1. * , count( e2.empid ) AS c FROM employees e1 LEFT JOIN employees e2 ON e1.dept = e2.dept GROUP BY e1.empid ORDER BY c DESC

I got this result:

empid   dept    sal     c
emp001  d001    10000   3
emp004  d001    10000   3
emp002  d001    10000   3
emp006  d003    5000    2
emp005  d003    5000    2
emp003  d002    20000   1

And then you could of course sort on empid to get the emp002 before the emp004 etc :)

Edit: A better MySQL query would be with not selecting * elements and escaping all table and field names with backticks, something like this:

SELECT `e1`.`empid`, `e1`.`dept`, `e1`.`sal`, COUNT(`e2`.`empid`) AS `c` FROM `employees` `e1` LEFT JOIN `employees` `e2` ON `e1`.`dept` = `e2`.`dept` GROUP BY `e1`.`empid` ORDER BY `c` DESC, `e1`.`empid`
